Day 2, 10:00 Local Time, 08:00 GMT, 13:30 IST: Well how do you follow that up? A day of the most incredible twists and turns. A day where South Africa could've and probably should've run away with the game. They had the pitch and conditions to do so. They had two openers going great guns. They had the platform. But it rarely comes that easy in Test cricket, and certainly not against a team like Australia. For all the flak they got after leaving out Scott Boland and for opting to bowl, they roared back into the game, changing tactics, going to the short ball, and also leaning on a couple of brilliant performances from Nathan Lyon and Mitchell Starc. That was as good a demolition job as you'll see with the second new ball late in the day. There was a suggestion from Ackerman in the presser that the light wasn't good enough at that stage, and that they should've come off. But that decision is in the hands of the umps and they certainly didn't think so.

So it's all set up beautifully on what is another bright and sunny morning in Newlands. Australia's batting frailties were left brutally exposed in Gqeberha, and on top of that they don't have the services of Steve Smith to rely on over here. They've been forced to shuffle up their batting order in his absence, with Green slated in at four, Inglis at five, and Renshaw pushed up to open. There's lots of pressure to deliver, none more so than on Marnus Labuschagne who might well be fighting for his career.
